name: Padded / Gambeson
desc: Quilted cloth — cheap, quiet, and the layer worn *under* heavier armor. Barely there, but better than skin: it turns a blow, it never refuses one, so it has no **A** at all.

name: Leather
desc: Hardened hide. Turns a blow far better than cloth; no real penalty to wear all day.

name: Mail
desc: Interlinked rings — the pre-gunpowder workhorse, and the reason the gambeson has its own row: mail is worn *over* padding, not instead of it.

name: Plate
desc: Articulated full plate — the best pre-gunpowder protection, and the only pre-modern armor with any **I** rating at all (it was built in the century that met the first firearms). `M4 A2` is why a man in plate is not killed with a sword: you need a crossbow, a pick, or his visor. And it costs accordingly — 20 kg, a point of Coordination, a point of Perception under the helm, and the price of a small farm; see the Breastplate for where this ends up once guns make the rest of it not worth carrying.

name: Breastplate / Cuirass
desc: Plate over the chest and nothing else — the same steel as full plate, answering the three hits in ten that land on the biggest part of you. This is where armor **ended up**: once firearms made complete coverage not worth its weight, plate shrank to three-quarter, then to the cuirass, then to a *gorget* (neck and upper chest alone, 1 kg, 100). All three are this row with an adjective, and every one of them is a deliberate trade of coverage for weight, money and the ability to move.

name: Helmet
desc: Open-faced helm — the single best value in armor, because the head is the worst place to be hit and nobody is born with a skull worth `M3`. `G5` is the price of seeing and breathing: half of all head hits find the face. *Visored* closes it to `G2` and costs another point of PC; a *mail coif* is `M2 A0 G5`; a *steel field helmet* (TL 4¼) is `M3 I2 A1 G4`, and a *modern ballistic helmet* (TL 6) is `M3 I3 A1 G2`. The field helmet was never meant to stop a rifle round and doesn't — it was meant to stop **shell fragments**, which is why the helmet is the piece of armor that came back first.

name: Shield
desc: Not worn but wielded — a Parry PM and cover you can point at the threat. Costs you a hand; see Melee Combat.

name: Ballistic Vest
desc: Concealable soft armor — stops handgun rounds and fragments, does little against a rifle. `I3 A1`: a pistol hit that lands is usually one wound level or none at all, and a 7.62 goes through it regardless.

name: Tactical Armor
desc: Soft armor plus rifle-rated hard plates. Bulky, hot, and the difference between a wound level and a funeral.

name: Riot Gear
desc: Built for the melee end — batons, thrown objects, a crowd pressing in. `M4 A2` makes it very nearly immune to all of that, and it has almost nothing to offer against a bullet.

name: Combat Armor
desc: Composite hard-shell suit with its own air — the SF soldier's plate. Light for what it stops; the helm still costs you some perception.

name: Powered Armor
desc: Motorized exoskeleton — the servos carry the weight *and* add strength, so the penalty inverts. Uses Damage Scale; a walking vehicle you wear.
